text:
Mike O: Heads-up — started seeing GPU hosts flip into 'driver failed' after the node image rollout to kernel 6.2.0-23 on us-west yesterday evening. ~30% of g4/g5 nodes show nvidia module load errors.
Leming: Ugh. Any obvious dmesg traces?
Mike O: Pasted a couple lines from one affected host: 
```
[  142.123456] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel.
[  142.123459] nvidia: Unknown symbol amdgpu_device (err 0)
[  142.123470] NVRM: loading NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module 525.105.17 Tue Jan 10 2024
[  142.123480] NVRM: API mismatch: the client has the version 525.105.17, but the kernel module has the version 525.90.02.
[  142.123490] nvidia-nvlink: Nvlink core is unavailable.
```
Sarah J: API mismatch could be DKMS build against older kernel headers or missing symbols from new kernel ABI. Did the node image bump driver or kernel independently?
Mike O: Image changed kernel -> 6.2.0-23. Driver was pinned to 525.105.17 in the image. Some hosts show modprobe errors: "Unknown symbol nvidia_get_fence".
Ryan T: We also saw similar after 5.15 -> 6.x on staging last month but I thought that was resolved by re-building the driver against the new headers. Did DKMS run?
Mike O: DKMS logs show build failed on some nodes: /var/lib/dkms/nvidia/525.105.17/build/make.log contains undefined reference to `__crc32c_generic` and then it aborts.
Leming: That CRC symbol is an in-kernel symbol that moved/export changed between 5.15 and 6.x kernels. Some vendor drivers expect it in a different place. If DKMS can't link, modules won't load.
ops-bot: Incident created: INF-4821 — kernel 6.2 rollout causing nvidia module failures in us-west (severity: high).
Sarah J: Quick triage plan:
- Pin new node images to kernel 5.15 for production pools in us-west/eu-west until we have validated driver rebuilds.
- Collect a matrix of kernel -> driver -> cuda -> NCCL combos that fail.
- Try building 525.105.17 vs 535.x against 6.2 headers; if 525 cannot build, try 535 series (note driver version compatibility with CUDA 11.8/12.1).
Mike O: On a handful of repro hosts I tested: 525.x fails to build on 6.2; 535.86 builds but then CUDA 11.8 runtime has warnings and some tests in our perf suite fail (runtimes up, some kernels segfault).
Ryan T: So two regressions: driver vs kernel ABI, and downstream CUDA/NCCL oddness with newer driver. We need to avoid surprising customers — rollback/pin is safest.
Leming: Cost/impact: about 120 GPUs out of ~400 in us-west/eu-west pools affected across burst capacity — that's ~30% capacity reduction and some queued jobs failing.
Sarah J: Action items:
- @infra-team: immediately pin the boot image for dedicated and hosted nodes to kernel 5.15 and rollback the pushing image in us-west (rollback planned in next 30m).
- @infra-ops: collect /var/log/dkms*, uname -r, modinfo nvidia, and dmesg snippets from 10 failing hosts and upload to INF-4821.
- @platform: block the auto-image-rollout pipeline until a compatibility matrix is added to the pre-release checks.
Mike O: I'll start a small canary build: try driver 535 + CUDA 12.1 in staging with kernel 6.2 and run our E2E perf + functional tests. If it passes we can plan a controlled upgrade with node draining and canaries.
Ryan T: Also note: older nodes with prebuilt container images that have a bundled driver will still fail if host module mismatches. We should add a host-driver-version header to the node metadata so scheduler avoids pulling tasks that require specific drivers.
Leming: For the short-term mitigation I pushed a host-level reconciliation: nodes failing nvidia modprobe get cordoned and drained; autoscaler will not spin new 6.2 nodes in affected pools.
ops-bot: INF-4821 updated — rollback started at 1717995100, pinned kernel=5.15.0-101 for us-west images.
Sarah J: Good. Postmortem dev notes: record exact kernel symbols that changed, update our node image build to run a DKMS build + CUDA test matrix as part of the release gate, and add a preflight that checks /proc/kallsyms exports we depend on.
Mike O: I'll attach test outputs to INF-4821 and follow up with a proposal to support driver bundles built for multiple kernel targets.
Ryan T: Ping me when you have the canary results. I'll handle a customer communication draft for those on Dedicated with nodes in us-west.
Sarah J: Thanks team — let's aim to have rollback complete and a status update to incident channel in 45m. :thumbsup:
